newsitem.title: CHINA: China stable in post-Deng era, premier says.
newsitem.headline: China stable in post-Deng era, premier says.

text.p: China's Premier Li Peng said on Friday the country's political situation was stable after the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, but avoided mention of recent bomb attacks in Beijing and western China.

Judging from the proceedings of the National People's Congress, or parliament, "we can see that... China's political situation is stable", Li told a news conference after the annual session of parliament ended in Beijing.
"We are convinced that... China's situation will become better and better," he said.
Li pledged allegiance to Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin, anointed heir to Deng, who died on February 19 at the age of 92.
"The current collective leadership with comrade Jiang Zemin at the core has the support of the entire Chinese people," the premier said.
Li made no mention of bomb attacks in Beijing and Urumqi, capital of the restive region of Xinjiang, that followed Deng's death.
Two bombs exploded in Beijing last week. One of the attacks killed two people and wounded about 30, sources have said.
Three bombs went off on public buses in the Xinjiang regional capital Urumqi on February 25 in an attack apparently timed to coincide with funeral rites in Beijing for Deng.
Nine people were killed and 74 wounded.

Exiled ethnic Uighurs, who want to set up an independent state of "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, have claimed responsibility for the bombings and vowed to stage more attacks until they gain complete freedom for their homeland.
Police and other officials have said there was no evidence linking those bombings with unrest in Xinjiang.

But taxi drivers in the Chinese capital have said they have been asked not to give rides to suspicious looking people from Xinjiang and to be especially cautious in neighbourhoods where many Uighur migrants live.
